name: Example: Differentiating Inverse Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions Using the Quotient Rule
worked_solution:
Here, we let $u(x) = \textrm{arcsec } x$ and $v(x) = \textrm{arccsc } x$, and apply the quotient rule.

We use the formulae

$$
u'(x) =  \dfrac 1 {|x| \sqrt {x^2 - 1}}	\quad \text{and} \quad	v'(x) = -\dfrac 1 {|x| \sqrt {x^2 - 1}}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}\cdot \text{arccsc }x-\text{arcsec }x\cdot (-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}})}{{\text{arccsc }}^{2}x} \\  & =(\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}})\frac{\text{arccsc }x+\text{arcsec }x}{{\text{arccsc }}^{2}x} \\  & =\frac{\text{arccsc }x+\text{arcsec }x}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}{\text{ arccsc }}^{2}x}.\end{aligned}
$$
